compareCandidate.label: Decomposer vs. consumer
compareCandidate.description: A consumer eats living things. A decomposer breaks down things that are already dead - fallen leaves, dead animals - and returns their materials to the soil.

plainLanguageExplanation: A decomposer breaks down dead things - fallen leaves, dead animals, and waste - and returns their materials to the soil. Fungi, bacteria, and earthworms are the main decomposers. As they eat and break down dead matter, they release nutrients like nitrogen and minerals back into the soil, where plants can use them again. Decomposers are the ecosystem's recyclers: without them, nutrients would stay locked up in dead bodies and the soil would slowly run out of the materials life needs.

whyItMatters: Decomposers close the loop in every ecosystem - they return dead materials to the soil so nutrients can be used again. Understanding them explains why the ground does not pile up with dead things and how soil stays rich.
didYouKnow: A single teaspoon of soil can hold more than a billion bacteria - a whole world of decomposers working under your feet.
